name: New Mexico
overview: In New Mexico the state, not the county, sells real property for delinquent property taxes: the Taxation and Revenue Department's Property Tax Division (PTD) holds public auctions county by county. There is no set schedule, and the PTD does not hold a sale in every one of the 33 counties each year. Bidding is oral and in person, starting from a minimum bid equal to the taxes, penalty, interest and costs due, and the state issues a tax deed equivalent to a quitclaim deed. New Mexico has no right of redemption for former owners after the sale, but a former owner has two years to challenge the sale in court; all sales are final.

The minimum bid is based on the total of taxes, penalty, interest and costs due.
The state issues a tax deed equivalent to a quitclaim deed.
The State of New Mexico does not have a Right of Redemption for former owners.

counties.next_sale_note: No upcoming Bernalillo County sale posted. As of 2026-10-27 the Property Tax Division's auction schedule lists only San Miguel County (Nov 19, 2026); the Division says there is no set schedule and it does not hold sales in every county each year.
counties.how_to_bid: Register at the auction on sale day (registration opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 10 a.m. when the auction starts). Bidding is oral; bidders must be present or represented by an agent. The minimum bid is the total of taxes, penalty, interest and costs due. Payment by cashier's check, money order, or personal or company check only with a letter of guarantee. The state issues a tax deed equivalent to a quitclaim deed; sales are final with no refunds.
